chapter: Return to Basie and leaving in 1948
title: Lester Young at Camp Gordon, playing all day in the rec hall
summary: Jones says Lester left the Army before him and was kept playing in the rec hall at Camp Gordon, put back in the prisoner area each night.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Did Pres ever come back when he came out?

No, he did not. See, Lester beat me out of the Army and by that time, when Lester came out of the Army, I was at Fort Ord and they gave me a pass to go down to visit with Lester. See because at the time that Lester Young was in Camp Gordon, the general of the post loved Lester Young, you see, and we were trying to get Lester Young from that place and that's when I ran into the bass player which they had deposed, sent him somewhere to Camp Stewart, but a trumpet player took over to be the MP to look over Lester. Lester wound up, like I said, with about 15 pieces. All day long he was playing his horn and then at the end of the day they put him back on the other side of the tracks like he'd been digging ditches, but he wasn't. Somebody would always stand at the window and watch for somebody to come into the Rec Hall or Recreation Hall to see if any officers came over. When Norman got in touch with me - because at that time the general told me to get in touch with Basie. I called Basie up. Basie was playing the Roxy Theatre but he was at the barbershop.
I was in Fort Ord at the time.
